title: Section 25 HMA — Permanent alimony and maintenance

content.overview: Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is permanent alimony and maintenance. At the time of passing any decree under the Act, or at any time afterwards, the court may on application order the respondent to pay the applicant a gross sum, or a monthly or periodical sum for a term not exceeding the applicant's life. The court has regard to the respondent's income and other property, the applicant's income and other property, the conduct of the parties, and other circumstances. The payment may be secured by a charge on the respondent's immovable property. The court may vary, modify or rescind the order on a change of circumstances. It may also do so if the favoured party remarries, or if the wife has not remained chaste, or if the husband has had sexual intercourse with any woman outside wedlock.
content.study: Use section 25 only with a decree under the Act, or after such a decree. Either spouse may apply. Record income, property and conduct before the sum. Do not treat a section 24 order as this order.

learningObjectives: Tie section 25 to a decree under the Act.
List the quantum factors and the charge.
State the variation and rescission grounds.
enhancement.definition: Section 25 is the court's power, on or after a decree under the Act, to award either spouse a gross or periodical sum for maintenance, secured if necessary.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Permanent alimony follows a decree. It is revisable on a change of circumstances and on the conduct grounds in subsection (3).
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, section 25. Section 24 is pendente lite.
essentialIngredients: Decree under the Act, or a later application after such a decree
Gross sum or monthly or periodical sum
Term not exceeding the applicant's life
Regard to both parties' income and property, conduct, and other circumstances
Variation on changed circumstances or subsection (3) conduct
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The jurisdiction is any court exercising jurisdiction under the Act. The timing is the decree, or any time subsequent. The applicant may be the wife or the husband. The order is against the respondent. Quantum is what seems just after the stated factors, not a fixed share. The sum may be gross or periodical, and a periodical sum cannot be ordered for longer than the applicant's life. Subsection (2) allows variation, modification or rescission if circumstances change. Subsection (3) allows the other party to seek variation, modification or rescission if the favoured party has remarried, if she has not remained chaste, or if he has had sexual intercourse outside wedlock. A dismissal that is not a decree granting relief still has to be checked against the words 'any decree'; this note does not adopt a case on whether every dismissal qualifies.
examples: A divorce decree is passed. The wife applies for a monthly sum. The court regards both incomes, property and conduct.
The husband later remarries. The wife may seek variation or rescission under subsection (3).
Only a section 24 application is pending and no decree has been passed. Section 25 timing is not yet met.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm a decree under the Act, then apply the factors. Use subsection (2) or (3) only for a later change or the stated conduct.
distinctions: Section 25 permanent alimony vs section 24 pendente lite
Variation for change of circumstances vs subsection (3) conduct
Either spouse vs a wife-only award
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Cooling-off waiver and cruelty tests remain on the case-law gate.
enhancement.shortAnswerStructure: On or after a decree, either spouse may be awarded a just gross or periodical sum, revisable on changed circumstances or the subsection (3) grounds.
enhancement.tenMarkStructure: Timing → factors → charge → variation and rescission → border with section 24.
enhancement.sixteenMarkStructure: Permanent alimony → who and when → quantum → security → subsections (2) and (3) → facts → conclusion.

keyTakeaways: Section 25 needs a decree under the Act, or an application after it.
Income, property, conduct and other circumstances are regarded.
The order may be secured on immovable property.
Remarriage or the stated conduct can support rescission.

verification.note: Section 25 text only. No holding on whether a bare dismissal is a decree.
